text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some ministers are expected to head National Democratic Rally party candidate lists in June parliamentary elections. The party groups staunch supporters of the government.

- Berber Spring overshadowed by divisions among grass-root supporters of mainly Berber parties. Berber activists on April 20 mark the Berber Spring, recalling government repression 17 years ago when security forces clashed with Berber activists in Tizi-Ouzou and other Berber-dominated areas in northeastern Algeria. The activists want the government to recognise their native Tamazight tongue as an official language alongside Arabic.
- Former ruling National Liberation Front has not yet decided who will lead the party lists in the legislative elections in some provinces.
- Secular opposition Socialist Forces Front denies speculation that the party's self-exiled leader Hocine Ait Ahmed might return to Algiers to lead the party list in the Algerian capital.

- Former prime minister Mouloud Hamrouche raps his National Liberation Front (FLN) party leadership for allegedly excluding reform-minded candidates in the party lists in some towns. Hamrouche is seen as the leader of a FLN wing advocating a sharpened opposition stand against the government.
